verdicts.evidence: Discord row (script, not in ledger). ConductAtlas quotes: 'We may disclose information if Discord is evaluating and/or engaging in a merger, acquisition, reorganization, bankruptcy, or sale, transfer, or change in ownership of Discord or any of its assets.' Word for word. Date printed in the policy: Sept. 29, 2025. Captured 19 April 2026; checked 5 Oct 2026.

DraftKings row (script). ConductAtlas quotes: 'In the event of an insolvency, bankruptcy, or receivership, your personal information may also be transferred as a business asset.' Word for word. Date printed in the policy: May 21, 2025. Citation capture 13 September 2026 (first captured 19 April 2026).

Character.AI row (script). Straight Arrow News, 13 October 2026: the policy 'allows Character.AI to share user information during a "sale of company assets"'; it 'says the company may disclose "certain information" during the negotiations or the closing of a merger, sale of company assets'. The article says the company filed for Chapter 11. Matches the home claim and its REPORTED tag.

Spotify row (script). The quotation and date hold: TOS Tracker's copy reads 'If we were to sell or negotiate to sell any part of our business to a buyer or possible buyer. In this case, we may transfer your personal data to a successor or affiliate as part of that transaction.' and 'Effective as of July 1, 2026' (the page's ellipsis stands for 'In this case,'). But 'The tracker found no mention of bankruptcy' credits the tracker with a finding it does not make. The tracker says nothing on the subject; the word is simply absent from its captured text ('bankruptcy', 'insolvency' and 'merger' not found).
verdicts.fix: Policy effective 1 July 2026, as captured by TOS Tracker. The captured text does not contain the word bankruptcy (our search of the tracker's copy, 10 November 2026).

verdicts.evidence: Amazon row (script). Both quoted fragments are word for word, joined in the source by the word 'but' as on the page. Date stated by the document: June 30, 2026. Citation capture 13 September 2026.
Toysmart row (script). CNN Money, 21 July 2000: 'The statement, posted on Toysmart's Web site, stated that such information would never be shared with third parties.'

flags: Live policies: none could be read. discord.com/privacy, draftkings.com/privacy, spotify.com/us/legal/privacy-policy and the Amazon privacy notice on amazon.com were all refused by this session's fetch allowlist. Every tracker quotation was confirmed at the tracker. Whether each live policy still reads this way today is UNKNOWN; the page's own WATCH tag says as much.
The fetch tool returns quotations in pieces of 125 characters or fewer, so each long sentence was confirmed in two reads and joined. The joins are noted in the evidence.

Amazon: an Amazon-hosted copy of the notice (payeecentral.amazon.com) carries the same business-transfers clause but shows 'Last updated: February 14, 2025'. ConductAtlas gives 30 June 2026 as the date stated by the document it captured. The page's date matches the tracker; the difference between the two copies was not resolved.

Amazon's clause goes on to say that if Amazon.com, Inc. or substantially all of its assets are acquired, customer information 'will of course be one of the transferred assets'. The row's label 'Carries its promises forward' is fair to the sentence quoted, but the page does not show the sentence after it.
ConductAtlas notes that its summaries are generated by a model and not read by a person. Only the quoted policy text was relied on, not the summaries.

Spotify: TOS Tracker lists the version under 10 July 2026 as its capture date and says that is 'not a claimed legal effective date'. The policy text itself says 1 July 2026, which is what the page gives.
The extractor sees only 5 claims. The six audit rows live in a script array, each rendered with a REPORTED tag; they are judged as s01 to s06. c002 is a duplicate of c001.

Room 1 opens 'The Estate Sale found that ... the law slows a sale of your data mainly if the company had promised not to transfer it.' That sentence is tagged INFERENCE at home ('from 11 U.S.C. 363(b)(1)'); here it is untagged and introduced as a finding. Suggest 'The Estate Sale argued' and an INFERENCE tag.

The audit summary ('a court must bring in a privacy ombudsman when a sale would break a promise not to transfer') is tagged INFERENCE here and REPORTED at home. Weaker, so no tag problem. The Estate Sale's earlier check noted that the U.S. Trustee reportedly calls Character.AI's policy ambiguous and says an ombudsman is required; the 'harder to pull' line for Character.AI is contested.
The page says 'Here are five, with the words as captured by policy trackers.' There are six rows; two (Character.AI and Toysmart) are from news reports, not trackers, as the note below does say.
'Woven from' lists Brief 006, The Bankruptcy Estate of You, but no claim on the page is drawn from or linked to it.
c005 rests on the home page; '... and lost' means the judge overruled the objections. Whether any state later appealed was not checked.

Editorial Standard: a real other side is present. Character.AI, an AI company, is a named subject; the page has the 'Researched and compiled with Claude (Anthropic)' line but no Anthropic conflict note. The home page, The Estate Sale, carries one.
